newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES AT THE WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHES AT THE WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league (kick-off times 1500 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Arsenal (2) v Aston Villa (5)

Arsenal hope to recover after a dismal 0-0 draw against Sheffield Wednesday on Thursday when coach Arsene Wenger, upset by an evening kick-off, failed to appear at a news conference. He may face disciplinary action.
Former England captain David Platt, who was ineffective, may be dropped with Paul Shaw, his second-half replacement at Sheffield, taking his place. Defender Martin Keown faces a fitness test.

Villa, whose five-match winning streak was ended by a 2-0 home defeat by Chelsea, could make changes. Coach Brian Little must decide between Balkan forwards Savo Milosevic and Sasa Curcic or Britons Tommy Johnson and Mark Draper.
Chelsea (7) v Sheffield Wednesday (10)

Chelsea, who kept their first clean sheet in 17 premier league games at Aston Villa, retain Welsh veteran Mark Hughes and Italian Gianfranco Zola despite Gianluca Vialli's return to fitness. Scott Minto, Frank Leboeuf and captain Dennis Wise, all fit, are also fighting to return.
Sheffield Wednesday, enjoying an unbeaten run which has lifted them into the top half, may still be without midfielder Graham Hyde who has hamstring trouble.
Coventry City (15) v Middlesbrough (17)

In-form Coventry, with three wins in a row, will probably be unchanged after their 3-1 win at Leeds on Thursday. Striker- turned-defender Dion Dublin reluctantly continues in a three-man defence while Darren Huckerby, scorer of two goals in three games, plays alongside Noel Whelan in attack.
Middlesbrough, whose 4-2 win over Everton ended a run of 12 without a win, will retain veteran Welsh international midfielder Clayton Blackmore, after he scored.
Derby (12) v Blackburn Rovers (18)

Derby hope to bounce back from disappointing defeats at Southampton and Sunderland. Manager Jim Smith should have Ireland defender Paul McGrath and striker Dean Sturridge back to full fitness after their half-fit recent efforts.

Blackburn, who gained their third win under caretaker coach Tony Parkes by beating Newcastle 1-0, hope to climb out of the bottom three. They are expected to be at full strength with Chris Sutton leading the attack and wearing the number nine shirt for only the second time since England striker Alan Shearer's transfer to Newcastle.
Everton (8) v Wimbledon (4)

Everton suffered only their second away defeat of the season at Middlesbrough on Thursday but hope to recover against tough Wimbledon. They will be without captain Dave Watson, who fractured a rib. His place will go to David Unsworth or Craig Short. England full-back Andy Hinchcliffe is out for the rest of the season with damaged knee ligaments.
Wimbledon hope to bounce back after a 5-0 hammering at Aston Villa last Saturday, their first defeat in 19 games.
Leicester City (13) v Nottingham Forest (20)
Buoyed by a 1-1 draw at Liverpool on Boxing Day, Leicester hope to begin climbing the table against their troubled rivals who were thrashed 4-0 at home by Manchester United.
Leicester hope midfielder Neil Lennon, who starts a two-match ban after this match, signs off with an inspired display but have doubts about Swedish defender Pontus Kaamark's hamstring.
Forest, under player and caretaker coach Stuart Pearce, may be without on-loan Nigel Clough, who broke his nose against United.
Manchester United (3) v Leeds United (14)

After hitting nine goals in two games, United are unbeaten in seven and are the bookmakers' second favourites for their fourth title in five years. Striker Andy Cole, who returned as a goalscoring substitute at Forest, could start in place of Ole Gunnar Solksjaer, who also struck on Boxing Day.

Leeds' run of five clean sheets came to an end on Thursday when they were beaten unexpectedly by Coventry. Coach George Graham has to rebuild morale again and decide whether to risk selecting Ghanaian striker Tony Yeboah, back from injury, in a game when they are likely to be defending for long periods.
Newcastle United (6) v Tottenham Hotspur (9)

Newcastle have taken only four points from the last 21 available and have gone seven games without a win but are still among the title contenders. French winger David Ginola and Colombian striker Faustino Asprilla remain doubtful.

Tottenham, for whom Norwegian stiker Steffen Iversen hit two goals against Southampton (his first for the club), may give John Scales his full debut after appearances as substitute following his transfer from Liverpool.
West Ham United (16) v Sunderland (11)
Injury-hit West Ham may retain on-loan striker Mike Newell in attack at the expense of Romanian Florin Raduciouiu in their first outing since losing 3-1 at Chelsea last Saturday.

Sunderland beat Derby 2-0 on Boxing Day when captain Kevin Ball broke his jaw. He will be out for six weeks and his replacement at West Ham could be Martin Smith as coach Peter Reid attempts to juggle his resources.
Southampton (19) v. Liverpool (1) (Sunday 1600 GMT)

Well-beaten at Tottenham on Thursday, Southampton face a daunting task in attempting to hold Liverpool's attack. The Saints have conceded 36 goals in 19 games and the leaders may have England striker Robbie Fowler back after missing the game against Leicester.
